athlete.name: Luke
context: Ran Grandma's Marathon 6/20/2026 in 3:45:49 - GI distress during the race; pre-race training projection was ~3:28.
3-4 week layoff after Grandma's for illness + sore Achilles.
Half marathon PR: 1:30. Ran this exact Cambridge course in 11/2025 in 1:35.

Goal of 1:28 is a real but ambitious target given demonstrated sub-1:30 fitness - not supported by the marathon-day result alone (GI issues), so paces below are set from the PR/Cambridge-2025 evidence and will be recalibrated after the Week 8 time trial.

weeks.focus: Return to running, calm the Achilles down, no pace targets
coach_notes: Your ACWR is sitting at 1.5 and training status read 'unproductive' the week I pulled your Garmin data - that's the load spiking faster than your body is absorbing it. This week undoes that: everything is capped at conversational effort and the Achilles work is daily, not optional.
No paces this week on purpose. Run by feel and heart rate (stay in Zone 1-2, 107-144bpm). If the Achilles is more than mildly achy the next morning, swap that day's run for the bike or rest.

sessions.title: Easy shakeout
sessions.details: Flat ground if you have it. Walk breaks anytime.

sessions.title: Daily Achilles work

exercises.name: Eccentric heel drop (Alfredson protocol)
exercises.prescription: 3 x 15 straight-leg + 3 x 15 bent-knee, both legs, daily
exercises.cue: Slow 3-count lower off a step, use the good leg (or hands) to reset up. Mild ache is fine, sharp pain is not.

sessions.note: Do this every day this week, not just on strength days.

sessions.title: Strength A - Prehab focus (Achilles/hip)

exercises.name: Achilles isometric calf hold
exercises.cue: Pain during the hold should stay <=3/10. Stop the exercise, not the plan, if it spikes.

exercises.name: Eccentric heel drop (Alfredson protocol)
exercises.prescription: 3 x 15 straight-leg + 3 x 15 bent-knee, both legs, daily
exercises.cue: Slow 3-count lower off a step, use the good leg (or hands) to reset up. Mild ache is fine, sharp pain is not.

exercises.name: Tibialis raise
exercises.prescription: 3 x 15-20, heels on a small plate or wall lean
exercises.cue: Builds shin/ankle strength that protects the Achilles as load climbs.

exercises.name: Banded clamshell
exercises.cue: Hip stability - keeps the knee tracking straight under fatigue.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance reach
exercises.cue: Cheap injury insurance - do it in socks on a hard floor.

sessions.note: This block's real job is the Achilles and hips, not the barbell. Keep everything else light.
